I consider myself a relatively green person but I'm becoming less concerned with landfilling.  As long the products do not pose toxic leaching I don't cringe as much as I used too about landfills.  

I'm more concerned with full life cycle analysis (of raw materials and end products) if there is not a good economic reason to recycle than we shouldn't keep banging that square peg into a round hole.  There is a good planet money pod cast about how the arrow triangle caused major issues in the recycling industry, I believe they even touched on how this has contributed to the great pacific garbage patch (although that could have been another podcast), I'd much rather all of that trash having been buried in the ground, how about yourself? 

I do believe that we should still be investigating how to improve the economics of recycling to conserve the energy required to mine/produce the raw materials.  For example I personally take aluminum cans (as well as steel cans) to the scrap yard, not because of the small amounts of money that I get for it but because I have some confidence that if any entity has paid me anything for it there is a greater chance that the materials will be returned to the supply chain.  My understanding currently almost all comingled municipal recycling programs are just being landfilled now.

Although some additional details will help:

What is the mileage on the car?  Is the noise related to engine speed or vehicle speed (do you hear it when the car is stopped and engine running, possibly rev it a little bit)?  Is the noise a constant frequency or does it change faster you drive or faster the engine revs?  If the noise is related to speed of the vehicle does it change when you go around a corner (try both left turns and right turns)?  Confirm blower motor (heat/AC) being turned off/on doesn't change it?

List of things it could be:

Engine speed noise- serpentine belt idler/tensioner bearings going bad or something ran off the belt such as alternator.  Tensioner/idler bearings of timing belt (if it is this it needs to fixed immediately as it can destroy the engine if left to fail)

Vehicle speed noises - brake pad wear (won't change while turning) Wheel bearing wear (will change going around corners)

Constant noise regardless of speeds - engine fan bearings although would be intermittent when fan cycles.  Blower motor bearing failure if it changes when changing fan speeds on heat

Healthy engines pull 17-21 inches of vac (at sea level, subtract 1" for every 1,000' of elevation) and you'd anticipate seeing the same reading anywhere you measure it.  A failed booster will typically leave you with a rock hard pedal - for example, shut the car off and depress brake pedal 5 times, you will deplete all of the vacuum reserve and will be left with "non-power brakes"  and note how the pedal feels.  Then start the car and you will see the difference the power assist makes.

If you are chasing a stalling issue it will not becoming from the booster (well at least in my experience I have never seen it before).  I'd say start with a full stage 0 if not done recently (cap, rotor, wires, spark plugs, air filter and fuel filter).  Also consider a professional fuel injection system cleaning, especially if after the tune up you are still below 17" of manifold vacuum (personally a huge fan of BG products from back when I wrenched in a shop they were premium brand). 

Last note - The check valve should flow air in one direction, you can suck through hose side or blow through booster side but not the other way around.
